verses.1: I first expressed my opinion regarding everything, oh Theophile. This is what Jesus began to do and to teach.
verses.2: He was delivered by the Holy Spirit, who had chosen him to be an apostle. He continued his mission until that day.
verses.3: And he also spent his life suffering in many hardships. He walked around for forty days, preaching about the kingdom of God.
verses.4: And together with them, he also told them not to leave Jerusalem. They were to wait for the message from their father that I had given them.
verses.5: For John baptized with water, but you should be baptized in the Holy Spirit. This should happen after many days have passed.
verses.6: Then those who were with them asked him, “Lord, will you restore the kingdom of Israel at this time?”
verses.7: He said to them, “It is not your knowledge of the times or seasons that is important; what matters is the time when the Father will act in his own power.”
verses.8: But may you receive strength from the holy spirit when he comes upon you. May you be witnesses to me in Jerusalem, and throughout all Judea and Samaria, until the end of the world.
verses.9: And as they said these things, a cloud appeared before them, and it covered him from their eyes.
verses.10: And as they watched, they were carried upward toward the heavens. Then, two men appeared before them, wearing white clothes.
verses.11: They also said, “Men of Galilee, why are you standing here looking up at heaven? This is Jesus, who has risen from among you. He will ascend into heaven in a certain way, just as you saw him being carried away into heaven.”
verses.12: At that time, they were brought back to Jerusalem from the mountain called Elaios. That’s the hill that overlooks Jerusalem from afar.
verses.13: And when they entered, they went up to the upper room. There were Peter, John, James, Andrew, Philip, Bartholomew, Matthew, James the Alpheus, Simon the Zealot, and Judas Iscariot.
verses.14: All of them were united in their prayers, along with the woman, Mary, the mother of Jesus, and his brothers.
verses.15: And on those same days, Peter stood among his brothers and said, “There were about sixty people who had different names.”
verses.16: Brothers, it is necessary to fulfill the promise that was made by the Holy Spirit through the mouth of David regarding Judas, who acted as an guide for those who arrested Jesus.
verses.17: Because it was determined by us, and it reduced the amount of money required for this service.
verses.18: This man, therefore, seized a place by taking advantage of his unfair treatment. He became a tyrant, and all his power was taken away from him.
verses.19: And it became known to all those who lived in Jerusalem. Therefore, that place was named Akeldama, which means “Place of Blood.”
verses.20: For it is written in the Book of Psalms: “Let his house become desolate; let no one live there.” And another shall take charge of his supervision.
verses.21: Therefore, in every moment during which those men who came with us were present, the Lord Jesus entered and left us.
verses.22: Starting from John’s baptism until the day he was taken away from us, let this be a witness to his resurrection together with us.
verses.23: And they stood there: Joseph, who was called Barsabbas, who was chosen by Jesus, and Matthias.
verses.24: And we, with respect, said, “You, Lord, who know the hearts of all people, let me choose one from these two.”
verses.25: To take up the position of this office and mission, without having Judas gone to that specific place first.
verses.26: And they gave them gifts. The gifts fell onto Maththias. They were also gathered together with the twelve apostles.
